result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that the current numbers fall short, both are honest about the small sample and the missing baseline, and both give the director usable wording. B wins on checking later: it adds a scenario re-test 2–4 weeks on and a lead or QA review of real tickets a few weeks after the course. A tracks job metrics at 30/60/90 days but never re-checks what agents remember, and its seven-metric list is slightly less focused. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and a same-week quiz don't show better job performance, and both offer realistic metrics checked at 30/60/90 days along with a script for the director. A wins because it explicitly suggests re-testing with realistic scenarios 2–4 weeks later and scoring real tickets. B relies only on performance metrics for that and doesn't propose a delayed knowledge check. B is a little stronger on what 12 people with no baseline can support, and its director script is ready to use as written, while A's has placeholders.
